paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

extraction.paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Section V experimental setup and Fig. 5 (per-core MTTF snapshot for the proposed approach versus baselines)
scenario.description: Thermal-cycling-aware runtime resource manager (reliability-aware mapping, thread scheduling and DPM) evaluated on a simulated 8x8 NoC-based many-core running 25 randomly selected PARSEC application executions. The setup is compared against a nominal baseline, MOC [14] and reliability-aware mapping [2]. The paper gives a 109 mm2 chip area in 16nm and a 90 W TDP, but no per-block coordinates or per-block powers.
scenario.architecture: 8x8 homogeneous mesh NoC many-core with a squared floorplan, Niagara2/SPARC cores, private L1 and distributed shared L2 caches, four memory controllers, 16nm, 109 mm2 chip area, 90 W TDP; per-core DVFS and PCPG
scenario.workload: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmarks, randomly selected and issued at runtime; 25 application executions per simulation
scenario.operating_point: TDP 90 W; thermal cycling model with Ea_TC=0.42 eV, b=2.35, Tth=1 C, k=8.62e-5 eV/K, A_TC fitted to give MTTF_TC=10 years at deltaT=20 C, Tmax=70 C, 1 hour, m=10; temperature sampled about every 1 s

original_setup.solver: Noculator shared-memory NoC many-core simulator (Intel PIN based) with McPAT/Lumos power and scaling parameters. HotSpot steady-state thermal model integrated in the simulator. Per-core temperatures sampled about every 1 s feed the rainflow and Coffin-Manson reliability model (pdf pages 3 and 5).
original_setup.optimizer: Heuristic reliability-aware resource management: an extension of MapPro mapping using the RAF affinity metric (VF*AF/(MF*TF)), temperature-deviation-sorted round-robin thread scheduling, and DPM that adds the avgAmplitude*maxT metric to MOC (pdf pages 4 and 5).
original_setup.controller: Runtime feedback controller on the global controller. It combines a Reliability Analysis unit (low-pass filter, rainflow counting, Miner's rule, MTTF_TC with a 1-2 hour long-term period), mapping, thread scheduling with a few-ms short-term period, and DPM. DPM uses a PID stage plus MOC multi-objective control for per-core DVFS and PCPG under the 90 W TDP (pdf pages 3-5).
original_setup.benchmark: Simulated 8x8 NoC many-core with a squared floorplan, 109 mm2 chip area, 16nm, TDP 90 W. Workload: 25 randomly selected multi-threaded PARSEC application executions. Compared against nominal baseline, MOC [14] and reliability-aware mapping [2] (pdf page 5).

thermal_observable.unit: years (per-core MTTF_TC derived from per-core temperature cycles)
thermal_observable.location: Per core of the 8x8 mesh, from per-core temperature sensors (Fig. 5 snapshot of cores' MTTF)
thermal_observable.aggregation: Reported as minimum, average and standard deviation of per-core MTTF_TC over the cores. The paper gives only relative improvements in the text (min +54%/51%/39%, avg +40%/21%/20% vs baseline/MOC/RA-mapping). No absolute value is extracted from the figure bars.

physical_mismatches.reason: No per-block floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) or per-block power is published, only total chip area (109 mm2) and TDP (90 W). A Studio steady-state 2D thermal model cannot be built without splitting total power by an unpublished rule.

The paper's output metric is thermal-cycling lifetime (MTTF_TC), computed from transient temperature traces, rainflow cycle counting and long-term aging history. It is not a steady-state temperature field, so a steady-state Studio solve cannot reproduce it.

The controller is a dynamic closed loop with PID/MOC DVFS, PCPG, runtime application mapping and thread scheduling at ms to hour timescales. A static Studio solve has no equivalent controller or optimizer behavior.
The workload is time-varying and random (PARSEC applications entering and leaving at runtime). The power map is therefore transient and not a single fixed operating point.

The original thermal solver is HotSpot embedded in the Noculator/McPAT/Lumos simulation flow, and the package and cooling configuration is not described in the paper. The solver, boundary conditions and cooling therefore cannot be matched.
The scenario is a planar 2D many-core. No 3D stacking or interposer is involved, so there is no 3D or interposer mismatch.

studio_assumptions: No complete published floorplan and power scenario exists, so no Studio floorplan is produced (empty floorplan).
Any Studio bundled package, material, TIM, heat sink or boundary-condition defaults would be Studio assumptions and not paper-derived, because the paper specifies none of them.
The result would be a steady-state temperature estimate and cannot replicate the paper's MTTF_TC, controller or simulator behavior. No exact replication is claimed.

methods.note: Text claims were checked against pages 3-5: the Reliability Analysis chain (low-pass filter, rainflow, Miner's rule, MTTF_TC), the RAF=VF*AF/(MF*TF) mapping, temperature-deviation-sorted scheduling, and MOC DPM extended with avgAmplitude*maxT. The percentage-to-comparator order is explicit ('respectively'), so the extraction's order-assumption caveat is unnecessary. Fig. 1, 5 and 6 were not visually verified because only extracted text is supplied.

code.note: No repository, code link or availability statement appears on pages 1-6, and the asset list is empty. The only URL is the ITRS bibliography entry [17]. Noculator, HotSpot, McPAT/Lumos and MOC code are cited only. The extraction correctly claims nothing here.

parameters.note: The Section V text on page 5 supports 109 mm2, 16nm, 90 W TDP, 8x8 cores, four memory controllers, Ea=0.42 eV, b=2.35, Tth=1 C, k=8.62e-5 eV/K, the A_TC fit (10 y, dT=20 C, Tmax=70 C, 1 h, m=10) and 25 applications. Page 3 supports the ~1 s sampling and the 1-2 h long-term period. Page 4 supports 'few milliseconds' (null is correct). The unit conversions are arithmetically correct. The fitted A_TC is not published.

findings.reason: The kind is labeled custom_2d_steady although steady_2d_relevant is false and the floorplan and power_w are empty. The paper's decisive features are transient temperature traces, rainflow cycle counting, long-term aging history, a closed-loop DVFS/PCPG/mapping controller and a random time-varying workload. Labeling it a steady 2D experiment implies a reproduction path that the evidence does not support. It should be an explicit not-reproducible or no-experiment designation.
Fig. 5 (per-core MTTF snapshots) and Fig. 6 are on pdf page 6, but the scenario and observable cite page 5. Only the text discussion of the percentages is on page 5.

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The deterministic gate failed on input validity: a custom_2d_steady experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, but the extraction supplied an empty floorplan and empty power. The gate also found evidence entries lacking valid page or pinned-asset locators, no cited thermal observable or regime, and unresolved adversarial and independent reviews. comparison_valid is false, so there is no Studio result to compare against the paper and no replication of any kind is claimed. The paper's observable is per-core thermal-cycling MTTF_TC. It comes from sampled transient temperature traces, rainflow counting and long-term aging under a closed-loop controller (mapping, scheduling, DVFS/PCPG) with a random PARSEC workload, simulated with HotSpot inside Noculator/McPAT/Lumos. A custom 2D steady run has no transient trace and cannot produce MTTF_TC or controller behavior. The paper reports only relative MTTF_TC gains (minimum +54%/51%/39%, average +40%/21%/20% vs nominal baseline/MOC/RA-mapping, assuming the percentages follow the baseline order), with no absolute years or temperatures. Even if a steady solve were run, no numeric comparison would be valid because location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match. At most, qualitative reasoning would apply: lower or more uniform temperatures and smaller cycle amplitudes should favor longer thermal-cycling lifetime.
limitations: Studio did not run; there is no simulated thermal result and the comparison is invalid.

No per-block floorplan geometry or per-block power is published, only the 109 mm2 total area, 16nm node, 8x8 squared layout and 90 W TDP. TDP is a budget cap, not an operating power, and splitting it by an unpublished rule would be invented input.
Regime mismatch: the paper's MTTF_TC derives from transient traces, rainflow cycle counting and aging history, whereas a custom 2D steady run has no transient trace.
Controller mismatch: the PID/MOC DVFS, PCPG, runtime mapping and thread scheduling closed loop (ms to hour timescales) has no equivalent in a static solve.
Workload mismatch: 25 randomly selected PARSEC executions give a time-varying power map, and the application list and seeds are unpublished.

Solver and boundary mismatch: the original used HotSpot within Noculator/McPAT/Lumos with unspecified package, heat spreader, TIM, heat sink, cooling and ambient; any Studio defaults would be assumptions, not paper-derived values.

Observable and aggregation mismatch: the paper reports per-core MTTF_TC (min, avg, std) as relative improvements only; absolute Fig. 5/6 values were not digitized, and the assignment of percentages to comparators relies on sentence order.

The gate also reported evidence entries lacking valid page or pinned-asset locators, no cited steady/transient regime, no linked code, config or data assets, and pending adversarial and independent review, so the extraction is not independently verified.
No exact replication is claimed or possible; the 3D/interposer mismatch is not applicable because the scenario is planar.
